Who is credited with discovering Glycerol?
Glycerol: Carl Wilhelm Scheele. Glycerol is a sugar alcohol with chemical formula C3H5(OH)3.
Who is credited with discovering Theory of relativity?
Theory of relativity: Albert Einstein. Special relativity applies to all physical phenomena in the absence of gravity.
Who is credited with discovering Sombrero Galaxy?
Sombrero Galaxy: Pierre Méchain. It is a member of the Virgo II Groups, a series of galaxies and galaxy clusters strung out from the southern edge of the Virgo Supercluster.

First coined as a term in 1852, this pattern of continued drinking despite its harms affected an estimated 283 million people worldwide as of 2016, according to the World Health Organization — name the condition?
Alcoholism is the continued drinking of alcohol despite the problems it causes.

Affecting roughly 1 in 15,000 people, this rare genetic disorder impairs the nervous system, causing severe intellectual disability and little to no speech, but is also linked to an unusually happy demeanor — what's it called?
Angelman syndrome (AS) is a rare genetic disorder that affects approximately 1 in 15,000 individuals.
Founder of a prominent Russian design studio and an avid, famously foul-mouthed blogger, this designer and entrepreneur is also a member of the Tolstoy family — name this designer?
Artemy Lebedev (born 13 February 1975) is a Russian designer, entrepreneur and Internet personality.
Marketed early on as the Debonair in its conventional-tail form, this piston single has been built continuously longer than any other aircraft ever made — which model?
Beechcraft Bonanza is an American general aviation aircraft introduced in 1947 by Beech Aircraft Corporation of Wichita, Kansas.
As Square's chief technology officer, this software engineer helped build Cash App before he was fatally stabbed in San Francisco in 2023 — who was he?
Bob Lee (businessman) (December 20, 1979 - April 4, 2023) was an American businessman and software engineer who was best known for helping to create the financial service Cash App.
Which winged insect fluttered into the fossil record around 56 million years ago and reaches adulthood only after pupating inside a chrysalis?

Butterfly are winged insects from the lepidopteran superfamily Papilionoidea, characterised by large, often brightly coloured wings that often fold together when at rest, and a conspicuous, fluttering flight.
This root vegetable owes its typical orange color to beta-carotene, though heirloom varieties can be white, purple, or even black — what vegetable is it?
Originating in Northern China, this spitz-type dog breed is known for a dense double coat that forms a distinctive ruff around the neck — name the breed?
Chow Chow is a spitz-type of dog breed originally from Northern China.
Though it resembles a barn swallow, this medium-sized bird is actually more closely related to hummingbirds than to any swallow, its resemblance being pure convergent evolution — what bird is it?

Common swift (Apus apus) is a medium-sized bird, superficially similar to the barn swallow or house martin but somewhat larger, though not stemming from those passerine species, being in the order Apodiformes.

This closed sac within the body has a distinct wall of cells that are structurally abnormal compared to surrounding tissue, and may contain air, fluid, or semi-solid material — unlike a pus-filled abscess, what is it called?
Cyst is a closed sac in the body, having a distinct envelope and division compared with the nearby tissue.
Bred around 1890 in Thuringia by a tax collector seeking a loyal protector, this German working-dog breed is known in North America by a slightly different two-word name — which breed?
Dobermann is a German breed of medium-large working dog of pinscher type.
Many of these Northern Hemisphere shade trees, prized along old European and American streets, were wiped out by a fungus carried by bark beetles — which tree genus is this?
Elm are deciduous and semi-deciduous trees comprising the genus Ulmus in the family Ulmaceae.
Distinct from secretion, this bodily process includes exhaling carbon dioxide, sweating, and passing urine through the bladder and urethra — what's it called?
Excretion is elimination of metabolic waste, which is an essential process in all organisms.
Sharing the 1962 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine with Maurice Wilkins, this English molecular biologist helped decipher the structure of DNA — who is he?
Francis Crick (8 June 1916 - 28 July 2004) was an English molecular biologist, biophysicist, and neuroscientist.
Often called the 'silent thief of sight' because it creeps up slowly, this group of eye diseases damages the optic nerve and is closely tied to raised pressure inside the eye — what is it?
Glaucoma is a group of eye diseases that can lead to damage of the optic nerve, which transmits visual information from the eye to the brain.
These seed-loving rodents come in 19 species, the golden or Syrian variety being the one most often found in a child's bedroom cage — what are they?
Hamster are rodents (order Rodentia) belonging to the subfamily Cricetinae, which contains 19 species classified in seven genera.

Despite resembling a common shellfish, this ancient arthropod is actually a chelicerate more closely related to spiders and scorpions, and is often called a 'living fossil' for its unchanged ancient body plan — what is it?
Horseshoe crab are arthropods of the family Limulidae and the only surviving xiphosurans.
Equal to one-twelfth of a foot and derived from the Roman word for 'twelfth,' this unit of length is often understood as roughly the width of a human thumb — name the unit?
Inch (symbol: in or) is a unit of length in the British Imperial and the United States customary systems of measurement.
Enlisting as a valet named 'Jean' on Bougainville's expedition, this expert botanist disguised herself as a man and became the first woman to sail all the way around the globe — who was she?

Jeanne Baret (27 July 1740 - 5 August 1807) was a French explorer, naturalist, and botanist who is recognised as the first woman to have completed a voyage of circumnavigation of the globe, which she did via boat.
Also called a kilopond, this deprecated gravitational metric unit equals exactly 9.80665 newtons — the weight of a one-thousand-gram mass under standard gravity. What is it?
Kilogram-force (kgf or kgF), or kilopond (kp, from Latin pondus, 'weight'), is a non-standard gravitational metric unit of force equal to the weight on Earth of a one-kilogram mass.

This group of blood cancers typically begins in the bone marrow and produces abnormal blood cells called blasts. Symptoms include bleeding, bruising, bone pain, and fever due to a lack of normal blood cells — what is this disease?
Leukemia (also spelled leukaemia) is a group of blood cancers that usually begin in the bone marrow and produce high numbers of abnormal blood cells.

With only six species left today, spread across Africa, South America, and Australia, this ancient group's fossil record stretches back over 410 million years to the Early Devonian — what group is it?
Lungfish are freshwater vertebrates belonging to the class Dipnoi.

Encompassing complex, functional, and measure theory as major subfields, this branch of mathematics studies real numbers, sequences, series, and limits with rigor formalized in the 19th century — which field?
Mathematical analysis is the branch of mathematics that studies functions, spaces, and operators through quantitative methods of approximation and convergence.
Carrying the NATO reporting name 'Halo,' this Soviet/Russian heavy transport helicopter is the largest of its kind ever to enter serial production — name the aircraft?
Mil Mi-26 is a Soviet/Russian heavy transport helicopter.
Likened to insulation on an electrical wire, this fatty material sheaths axon segments to speed up the transmission of nerve impulses — what is it called?

Myelin is a lipid-rich material that in most vertebrates surrounds the axons of neurons to insulate them and increase the rate at which electrical impulses (called action potentials) pass along the axon.
Nicknamed the 'winter vomiting disease' and the most common cause of gastroenteritis, this fecal–orally spread bug usually strikes about 24 hours after exposure. What is it?
Norovirus is the most common cause of gastroenteritis. Norovirus, also known as Norwalk virus, is the most common cause of gastroenteritis.
Triggered by a surge of luteinizing hormone near the midpoint of the cycle, this event sees an ovarian follicle rupture and release an egg ready to be fertilized. What's the term?
Ovulation is an important part of the menstrual cycle in female vertebrates where the egg cells are released from the ovaries as part of the ovarian cycle.
What medical term describes damage or disease affecting the nerves — impairing sensation, movement, gland, or organ function — commonly caused by systemic diseases such as diabetes?

Peripheral neuropathy is damage or disease affecting the nerves. Peripheral neuropathy may be acute (with sudden onset, rapid progress) or chronic (symptoms begin subtly and progress slowly), and may be reversible or permanent.
A member of the cashew family and a priority tree-nut allergen, this green seed saw the US, Iran, and Turkey produce 87% of the world's 1.4 million tonnes in 2024 — what is it?
Pistachio (UK also; Pistacia vera) is a small to medium-sized tree of the cashew family.
Including raccoons, coatis, kinkajous, and ringtails, this New World mammal family within the order Carnivora is made up mostly of omnivores — what family is it?
Procyonidae is a New World family of the order Carnivora. Procyonidae ( PROH-see-ON-i-dee) is a New World family of the order Carnivora.

This genus of roughly 1,750 flowering plant species, found worldwide mostly in temperate and mountainous regions, includes a tenacious creeping species common in European gardens as well as bulbous and meadow-dwelling relatives. What are these plants commonly called?
Ranunculus is a large genus of about 1750 species of flowering plants in the family Ranunculaceae.
Caused by two strains of human herpesvirus and nicknamed 'sixth disease,' this common childhood illness brings a rapid fever that gives way to a pink rash within days — what's it called?
Roseola is an infectious disease caused by certain types of human herpes viruses.
This marine plant group includes kelp, captures carbon, and generates over half of the planet's oxygen — what is it called?
Seaweed refers to thousands of species of macroscopic, multicellular, marine algae.
Once placed alone in the genus Uncia before phylogenetics moved it into Panthera, this high-altitude cat ranges across the Tibetan Plateau and Himalayas — what is it?
Snow leopard (Panthera uncia) is a species of large cat in the genus Panthera of the family Felidae.
This muscular, hollow organ in the upper digestive tract handles the gastric phase of digestion, and gives us the medical prefix 'gastric' from its Ancient Greek name — name the organ?
Stomach is a muscular, hollow organ in the upper gastrointestinal tract of humans and many other animals, including several invertebrates.

Tucked beneath the lateral fissure of the brain and named for its position near the head's temples, this region handles language comprehension, memory, and emotion — which part of the cerebral cortex?
Temporal lobe is one of the four major lobes of the cerebral cortex in the brain of mammals.

This field of geoscience studies the forms and features of land surfaces — not just elevation and relief, but also roads, boundaries, and buildings as recorded on detailed maps — what's this field called?
Topography is the study of forms and features of land surfaces. The topography of an area may refer to landforms and features themselves, or a description or depiction in maps.
As head of the WWII Office of Scientific Research and Development, this MIT engineer steered nearly all American military R&D, including radar and the early Manhattan Project — who was he?
Vannevar Bush (van-; March 11, 1890 - June 28, 1974) was an American engineer, inventor and science administrator, who during World War II headed the U.S.
The largest land-dwelling member of the weasel family, this solitary, muscular carnivore of the northern boreal forests can kill prey far larger than itself — what animal is it?
Wolverine (US also; Gulo gulo), also called the carcajou or quickhatch (from East Cree, kwiihkwahaacheew), is the largest land-dwelling member of the family Mustelidae.
Accidentally discovered in 1967 by German chemist Karl Clauss at Hoechst AG, which calorie-free artificial sweetener is sold under the brand names Sunett and Sweet One?

Designed to replace the Lockheed C-130 Hercules and sized between it and the Boeing C-17, this four-engine European turboprop military transporter first flew from Seville in December 2009 despite nearly being cancelled over cost overruns. What's the aircraft?
Airbus A400M Atlas: Multi-national four-engine turboprop military transport aircraft.
This mushroom genus contains the notorious 'death cap,' responsible for roughly 90% of all fatal mushroom poisonings worldwide — which genus?
Amanita: Genus of mushrooms. The genus is responsible for 95% of fatalities resulting from mushroom poisoning, with the death cap accounting for 90% of fatalities every year.
Consisting of a phenyl group attached to an amino group, this organic compound smells like rotten fish and serves as a key precursor to polyurethane and dyes — what is it called?
Aniline: Organic compound (C6H5NH2); simplest aromatic amine.
Native to alpine lakes and polar coastal waters, this cold-water relative of salmon holds the title of the world's most northerly freshwater fish — what is it?
This medical term describes the partial or complete wasting away of a body part due to poor nourishment, nerve loss, or disuse — what is the condition called?
Atrophy: Partial or complete wasting away of a part of the body. A diminished muscular trophic condition is designated as atrophy.
Produced continuously from 1964 to 2021, this line of twin-turboprop utility aircraft outsold all of its turboprop rivals combined — which aircraft family?
Beechcraft King Air: Twin engine turboprop aircraft family. The King Air line comprises a number of twin-turboprop models that have been divided into two families.

Despite its name, this snake is actually grey to dark brown — the name instead describes the dark interior of its mouth, displayed as a threat — which species, the second-longest venomous snake after the king cobra?
Black mamba: Species of venomous snake. The black mamba (Dendroaspis polylepis) is a species of highly venomous snake belonging to the family Elapidae.
Cattle, bison, buffalo, and goat-antelopes like sheep and goats all belong to this family of cloven-hoofed ruminants with over 140 living species — what is it?
Bovidae: Family of mammals belonging to even-toed ungulates.
In 1930, which Indian physicist won the Nobel Prize for discovering that light changes wavelength when passing through a transparent material, becoming the first Asian to win a Physics Nobel?

Defined by a –COOH functional group attached to an R-group, and only partially dissociating in water, this general class of organic compounds includes fatty compounds and the building blocks of proteins — what is this functional class called?
Carboxylic acid: Organic compound containing a –C(=O)OH group.
Often called the Judas tree, this small deciduous redbud native to Southern Europe and Western Asia bursts into deep pink blossoms each spring — what species is it?

Caused by a bacterium spread through contaminated water and undercooked shellfish, this intestinal infection produces severe watery diarrhea that can trigger dehydration within hours — which disease is it?
Cholera: Bacterial infection of the small intestine.
Recognizable by a prominent crest and curved bill, this Australasian parrot family includes 21 species, the smallest of which is the cockatiel — which family of birds?
Cockatoo: Any bird in the family Cacatuidae.
These colonial marine invertebrates secrete calcium carbonate to build the hard skeletons that form tropical reefs — what are they?
Coral: Marine invertebrates of the subphylum Anthozoa.
Named for the ancient Greek word for a ship's helmsman, this transdisciplinary field studies feedback loops and circular causal processes across engineering, biology, and social systems — what is it?

Cybernetics: Study of circular causal processes. Cybernetics' transdisciplinary character means that it intersects with a number of other fields, resulting in a wide influence and diverse interpretations.
This medical and surgical specialty treats everything from inflammatory conditions and cancers to hair loss, requiring about four years of training beyond medical school — what field is it?
Dermatology: Field of medicine dealing with the hair, nails, skin, and its diseases.
Developed from the civilian DC-3 airliner and nicknamed 'Dakota' by the RAF, which WWII transport plane hauled troops, cargo, and paratroopers for roughly 100 countries' militaries?
Douglas C-47 Skytrain: Military transport aircraft derived from DC-3.

Defined by permanently erect fangs at the front of the mouth and ranging from a 7-inch white-lipped snake to a nearly 19-foot king, which snake family includes most of the world's neck-flaring venomous serpents?
Elapidae: Family of venomous snakes. The family includes 55 genera with around 360 species and over 170 subspecies.

This Irish experimental physicist shared the 1951 Nobel with John Cockcroft for splitting the atom — the first nuclear transmutation, as the prize committee put it, "entirely under human control." Who was he?
Introduced to North America as early as 1840, this large eusocial wasp builds paper-like nests and preys on beetles, other wasps, and dragonflies — which insect is it?
European hornet: Species of wasp. The European hornet (Vespa crabro) is the largest eusocial wasp native to Europe.
The discipline that studies money, currency, assets, and liabilities, divided into personal, corporate, and public branches — what is this field of study called?
Finance: Academic discipline studying businesses and investments.

Sent by his father to work in a Manchester cotton mill, this German theorist co-wrote the Communist Manifesto with Karl Marx and later finished editing Das Kapital after his friend's death — who was he?
Friedrich Engels: German philosopher and socialist (1820–1895)

Working at Tuskegee Institute, this agricultural scientist urged cotton farmers to plant peanuts and sweet potatoes instead, publishing dozens of practical bulletins to fight soil depletion. Who is he?
George Washington Carver: American botanist and inventor (1864–1943)
This term describes the overall system of rules, processes, and power structures that steers decision-making within an organized group — what is it?
Governance: Processes of interacting with people and making decisions.
Occurring in any of the senses, this perception feels completely real despite the absence of any actual external stimulus — what is it?
Hallucination: Perception that only seems real.
With over 800 species lugging borrowed snail shells to shield their soft, non-calcified abdomens, this crustacean is essentially homeless without a hand-me-down home. What is it?
Stretching about a meter from crown to tail-tip, this deep-blue South American parrot is the largest of its kind and can be mistaken for a smaller relative — which vulnerable parrot?
Powered by four underperforming Lyulka turbojets, this aircraft became the first Soviet jet bomber to fly before being cancelled in September 1947 — which plane?
Ilyushin Il-22: 1947 Soviet bomber aircraft prototype. The Ilyushin Il-22, USAF/DOD designation Type 10, was the first Soviet jet-engined bomber to fly.
As president of the European Commission from 1985 to 1995, this French politician spearheaded the creation of the single market and laid the groundwork for the euro — who is he?
A real estate magnate and Spanish–American War officer worth roughly $87 million, he was the richest passenger aboard the Titanic — and went down with it in 1912. Who was he?
John Jacob Astor IV: American businessman and Titanic passenger (1864–1912)
This German-Finnish internet entrepreneur founded the file-hosting service Megaupload before U.S. authorities seized it in 2012 — who is he?

The smallest member of the genus Mustela, this slender carnivore has been introduced to New Zealand, Malta, Crete, the Azores, and São Tomé despite being native across Eurasia and North Africa — what is it?
Element number 3, this soft silvery-white alkali metal is the least dense metal of all and so reactive it must be stored under oil or in an inert atmosphere — what is it?
Lithium: Chemical element with atomic number 3 (Li)
Found in the hundreds inside most animal cells but almost never in plant cells, this acidic, enzyme-packed organelle serves as the cell's degradation center — which organelle?
Lysosome: Cell membrane organelle. A lysosome (/ˈlaɪsəˌsoʊm/) is a membrane-bound organelle that is found in all animal cells (except red blood cells), and rarely in plant cells.
The first Mexican-born scientist to win the Nobel Prize in Chemistry, this physical chemist shared the 1995 award for revealing how CFC gases threaten the ozone layer — who?
This mammal family — skunks and stink badgers — was reclassified out of the weasel family in the 1990s after genetic evidence, and turns out to be closest kin to red pandas and raccoons. What is it?
Mephitidae: Family of mammals. In taxonomic order, the living species of Mephitidae are:.

Codenamed 'Havoc' by NATO, this Soviet tandem-seat attack helicopter carries a single gun in an under-nose barbette and, unlike its predecessor, has no secondary troop-transport role. What aircraft is this?
Mil Mi-28: Russian attack helicopter. The Mil Mi-28 (NATO reporting name "Havoc") is a Soviet heavy-weight, all-weather, day-night, tandem-seat anti-armour military attack helicopter.
Its wings make an odd whistling sound on take-off, and one pair may raise up to six broods a year — which abundant North American gamebird?
Mourning dove: North American bird in the family Columbidae.
Descended from Southern Italy's traditional guard dogs and closely related to the Cane Corso, this large wrinkly Italian breed was recognized in 1949 — which dog breed?
Neapolitan Mastiff: Italian breed of dog. The Neapolitan Mastiff or Mastino Napoletano is an Italian breed of large dog of mastiff type.
Designed in the late 1950s as a six-engine, delta-winged prototype bomber capable of Mach 3+ at 70,000 feet, this aircraft was meant to outrun any interceptor of its era — which plane?
North American XB-70 Valkyrie: Prototype supersonic strategic bomber.
Mostly black on top, white below, and sporting unmistakable white eye patches, this cosmopolitan apex predator is actually the largest member of the oceanic dolphin family. What is it?
Orca: Largest living species of dolphin.

Named for its resemblance to a related crested dinosaur, this duck-billed herbivore could grow over 9 meters long, moved on two or four legs, and was first described in 1922 by William Parks — which dinosaur genus?
Parasaurolophus: Hadrosaurid ornithopod dinosaur genus from Late Cretaceous Period.
Created by Larry Wall in 1987 as a Unix scripting tool for report processing, this language's planned sixth version was eventually spun off and renamed Raku — which programming language?
Perl: Interpreted programming language first released in 1987.

A counting argument in mathematics: if you have more items than containers, at least one container must hold more than one item. Famous example: three gloves, but only two hand categories — what's this principle?
Pigeonhole principle: If there are more items than boxes holding them, one box must contain at least two items.
Looking like a jellyfish but actually a floating colony of cooperating zooids, this venomous siphonophore is also nicknamed the bluebottle — what is it?
Portuguese man o' war: Species of marine cnidarian.

This noncontagious autoimmune disease shows up as dry, scaly red or purple patches, and injuring the skin can trigger new lesions right at that spot — a quirk called the Koebner phenomenon — what is it?
Psoriasis: Autoimmune diseases of the skin. Psoriasis is a long-lasting, noncontagious autoimmune disease characterized by patches of abnormal skin.

Born Richard Alpert, this spiritual teacher researched psychedelics with Timothy Leary at Harvard before writing the 1971 bestseller Be Here Now, popularizing Eastern spirituality in the West. What name did he later take?
As chairman of Purdue Pharma, this physician-businessman oversaw the launch of OxyContin and was later portrayed in the miniseries Dopesick and Painkiller — who is he?

Formed by the fusion of five vertebrae between the ages of 18 and 30, this triangular bone sits at the base of the spine and connects to the tailbone below and the last lumbar vertebra above. What is it?
Sacrum: Bone of the spine. The sacrum situates at the upper, back part of the pelvic cavity, between the two wings of the pelvis.
This synthetic element, number 106, holds the rare distinction of being named after a scientist who was still alive at the time — its most stable isotopes survive mere minutes. What is it?
Seaborgium: Chemical element with atomic number 106 (Sg)

Usually caused by Staphylococcus bacteria and treated at home with warm compresses, this tender red bump at the edge of the eyelid is also known as a hordeolum — what is it?
Stye: Swelling of the eyelid due to infection of an oil gland.
Despite over a thousand species of this large hairy spider, many popular pet varieties defend themselves with irritating urticating hairs rather than a dangerous bite — which arachnid?
Best known for his 1651 work 'Leviathan' and its influential take on social contract theory, this English philosopher once met Galileo while tutoring the Cavendish family across Europe — who was he?
Thomas Hobbes: English philosopher and political theorist (1588–1679)

Occurring naturally in small amounts in dairy and meat but produced in large quantities by partially hydrogenating vegetable oils, this compound has been banned or tightly regulated in many countries — what is it, chemically speaking?
Trans fat: Type of unsaturated fat.
Element 124, also called eka-uranium, is a hypothetical g-block superactinide that may sit within the "island of stability" — what is its placeholder name?
Unbiquadium: Theoretical chemical element with atomic number 124 (Ubq)
Named by a naturalist in 1821, this family of feliform mammals split into genets, civets, and palm civets, and spans Africa to Southeast Asia — what is it?
Viverridae: Family of carnivorans. Viverridae is a family of small to medium-sized feliform mammals, comprising 14 genera with 33 species.
Nominated by Einstein, this Austrian physicist won the 1945 Nobel Prize for describing the exclusion principle and, in 1930, proposed the tiny neutral particle later named the neutrino — who is he?
The symbol for niobium is Nb. Niobium is a chemical element; it has symbol Nb and atomic number 41.
